NAME: OMat24 dataset
TYPE: component

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Training a TensorNet model on the 400 k‑structure MatPES‑PBE dataset requires approximately 15 minutes per epoch on a single RTX A6000 GPU, whereas training on the 100 M‑structure OMat24 dataset needs about 20 hours per epoch on sixteen A100 GPUs, highlighting the computational efficiency of MatPES.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The diversity of the larger OMat24 dataset does not benefit from the regularization or augmentation provided by DeNS, whereas dataset augmentation techniques like DeNS can significantly enhance performance when training solely on the MPtraj dataset.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Rattled systems in the OMat24 dataset have deleterious effects on model performance when evaluated on out-of-distribution hetero-diatomic systems.
ARTICLE: Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) Inorganic Materials Dataset and Models

DIRECT_CLAIMS: A single UMA model without any fine-tuning performs similarly or better than task-specialized models across diverse DFT tasks including materials, catalysis, molecules, molecular crystals, and MOFs.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: A novel two-stage training schedule with BF16 pre-training followed by FP32 fine-tuning recovers the 20-50% accuracy loss from BF16 precision alone while enabling efficient training.

NAME: Phonax (E(3)-equivariant graph neural network framework for phonon and Hessian prediction)
TYPE: method
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Phonax efficiently predicts phonon dispersion relations and density of states for inorganic crystal materials.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Including Hessian (second‑derivative) data in training improves the energy model accuracy beyond training with only energy and force data, reduces force MAE, and provides an effective ~7× increase in the amount of force information.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Augmenting a minimal 1×1×1 supercell training set with Hessian data yields more accurate phonon predictions than training on a larger 3×3×3 supercell alone.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The E(3)-equivariant graph neural network architecture automatically preserves crystalline symmetries, yielding the correct acoustic‑sum‑rule zero modes without additional corrections.
ARTICLE: Phonon predictions with E(3)-equivariant graph neural networks

NAME: Uncertainty quantification
TYPE: component
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Beyond‑DFT methods (HSE06, PBE0, G0W0, DMFT) are generated for a subset of materials to provide higher‑level reference data and enable uncertainty quantification.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The Gaussian process regression framework underlying GAP provides an uncertainty quantification that qualitatively estimates the potential’s accuracy for any given atomic configuration.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Uncertainty quantification based on latent‑space Euclidean distance provides error estimates that correlate with prediction errors, allowing exclusion of transitions whose uncertainty exceeds 50 % of the absolute free‑energy difference.
ARTICLE: Machine learning a general purpose interatomic potential for silicon

NAME: conservative models
TYPE: component

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Non-conservative models allow residual asymmetries to drive relaxation toward more stable close-packed structures, unlike equivariant models that remain trapped in symmetric but unstable configurations, though 70% (16%) of final configurations retain symmetry of initial structure with 0.01 Å threshold for conservative (non-conservative) models.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Elastic moduli predictions are very sensitive to the lack of energy conservation in MLIP models, and non-conservative models consistently perform worse on matbench-discovery downstream tasks despite achieving better training and validation accuracies.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: A two-step training strategy with direct force pretraining followed by conservative finetuning results in eSEN models with higher accuracy requiring less total training epochs and time compared to training conservative models from scratch.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Orb-v3-direct-20 uses only 32.8GB GPU memory for 100,000 atom systems and completes in under half a second, while all baseline methods and conservative models encounter Out Of Memory errors.
ARTICLE: Pushing the limits of unconstrained machine-learned interatomic potentials

TYPE: component

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Computing the frozen‑framework PES descriptors for 5997 Materials Project structures required seven days on a 48‑core CPU with two RTX 6000 GPUs, comparable to the time needed for ML‑driven MD on 100 materials.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Alternative ranking models (logistic regression L1/L2 and CatBoost) trained on PES descriptors, matminer descriptors, or their combination do not surpass the simple Ξ descriptor in predictive performance.
ARTICLE: Predicting ionic conductivity in solids from the machine-learned potential energy landscape

NAME: OMat24
TYPE: cited_work

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Fine-tuning models pre-trained on OMat24 to the MAD dataset achieves near-converged validation metrics in 30-100 epochs versus 700+ epochs when training from scratch, halving validation energy and force errors and achieving 50% lower test error than training on MAD alone.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: UMLIPs trained on the MatPES dataset achieve test mean absolute errors in energies that are 4–10 times lower than UMLIPs trained on the larger MPRelax or OMat24 datasets.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Across equilibrium, near‑equilibrium, and molecular‑dynamics property benchmarks, MatPES‑trained UMLIPs match or surpass the performance of models trained on much larger datasets such as OMat24 (≈100 M structures).

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Molecular‑dynamics simulations using MatPES‑trained UMLIPs exhibit markedly higher stability, with median termination temperatures up to ~1,900 K, versus ~1,300–1,500 K for MPRelax and OMat24 models.
ARTICLE: Orb-v3: atomistic simulation at scale
